races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Distillation
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on this surface and trainer Mark Usher has a quiet 14-day record (0/5); genuine hold-up horse whose best chance is getting a clear run in the straight — style fit discounted as it sits further forward than natural in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Distillation won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but his official rating of 53 and a nine and unplaced finishes in recent starts suggest he's inconsistent; the 133 lb burden from stall two adds another test.

runners_data.name: Athenian Spirit
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter by default, yet naturally a hold-up horse pressed into lead duties; nine runs with no wins tells its own story, but uncontested control at Southwell over 1m on Standard ground makes it dangerous to dismiss — Georgina Nicholls angle quiet (0/1 in 14 days).
runners_data.comment: Athenian Spirit was third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid grounding for conditions; yet to land a win in recent starts but at 131 lb from stall 10, our figures suggest he's well treated and merits respect.

runners_data.name: Hear The Drums
runners_data.note: Returns after 51 days off for Fahey yard, has one win over 7f on soft — a true rear-of-field traveller whose tendency to fade in the finish is a red flag, and it is squeezed into midfield rather than its natural position, reducing already modest prospects.
runners_data.comment: Hear The Drums won four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 66 marking him out as a strong threat from stall seven — though a trainer deep in a barren run of 0/42 is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Singarda
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood in form (2/11, 14-day); placed twice over 1m on Good and wears a tongue-tie — the most likely horse to push into a genuine prominent role naturally and benefit if a real pace develops.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in the field and 11 lb clear of his official mark on our ratings, Singarda has experience over today's trip and conditions and steps back up refreshed after 19 days off — the concern is he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Lady Fizz
runners_data.note: Three runs only, shortest priced newcomer profile, flagged as a fader in the finish — held up by nature but operates out of true position here; Dominique Van Der Kraats claims 7lb, which is the key positive to set against limited form and a fade pattern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with finishes of ninth, eighth and sixth in recent outings, Lady Fizz faces a stiff task here — our rating of 40 ranks her ninth of ten. She has run over today's trip and going before, but the form gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Miss Mambo
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (b) and returns 39 days fresh for Gay Kelleway; 3rd over 8f on soft is her best effort and she handles this surface, making her a dark horse if she can travel smoothly in mid-division from a natural hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Soda
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty in form (2/17 in 14 days) and Connor Beasley takes the ride — three third-place finishes show consistent placing but no win, and as a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield, its closing run will depend on a clear lane that may not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Soda does bring distance experience and a 28-day freshness angle, yet back-to-back thirds four and five starts back feel some time ago now, and that ninth last time out is hard to ignore; she has stall three and 130 lb to work with.

runners_data.name: Mist of Time
runners_data.note: William Knight in good form (4/17, 14 days) and Luke Morris is an upside angle; stepping back from 10f to 1m, but last three on this surface show regression — naturally races from the back, mapped to midfield, and needs something to go wrong at the front.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Mist of Time does arrive with some encouragement — third last time out and a fourth two starts back — though that eighth three starts back clouds the picture; she has run over today's trip and going, and 30 days between runs leaves fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Go Teejay
runners_data.note: Alex Jary claims 3lb and the horse wears a hood (p) for Craig Lidster (0/7 in 14 days); flags a fade pattern with three consecutive finishes in the 8-10 bracket, and racing 12 days fresh, it is among the least likely to benefit from this pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes of ninth, unplaced, sixth, eighth and eighth telling a bleak story, Go Teejay has run over today's trip and going before, but ranked eighth of ten on our figures, he is hard to fancy despite a quick 12-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Retro Rocket
runners_data.note: Only three runs to judge on — all on soft/good to soft or good — and this is a first run on Standard AW for Martin Keighley's juvenile; Harry Vigors claims 5lb which matters in a low-grade handicap, and as a genuine unknown on this surface, form projection is highly uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a string of mid-pack and unplaced efforts, Retro Rocket looks hard to fancy on our figures — ranked last of ten — though he has run over today's trip before and returns after a 33-day break with fitness on his side.

races.paceDynamic: Athenian Spirit is the one confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the lead from a natural hold-up profile, meaning this mile at Southwell AW is likely to be run at a measured, uncontested gallop with no genuine front-runner applying pressure from their natural inclination. The rest of the field is stacked with hold-up types — Distillation, Hear The Drums, Soda, Mist of Time, Go Teejay, and Retro Rocket are all true rear-of-field horses squeezed into a midfield mapping because the race simply cannot accommodate them all at the back, and they will be competing for the same closing ground in the straight. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get their natural position; Athenian Spirit is most likely to secure the front, with Singarda and Distillation the likeliest to push forward into a genuine prominent role if the pace is tepid. With a single, reluctant front-runner and a wall of closers chasing, the race shape most favours horses who can travel prominently off the slow pace and kick early — true hold-up finishers will face traffic problems and a lack of genuine pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Athenian Spirit Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Athenian Spirit is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a steady, controlled gallop throughout
scenarios.body: Athenian Spirit, racing out of natural role but mapped to the lead, controls the tempo and the field strings out behind on a flat Standard track; runners held up deepest face the most congestion turning in and the horse furthest forward at the two-furlong pole holds a decisive advantage

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If two or three horses push forward early and a proper pace develops, rewarding those just off the lead
scenarios.body: A genuine pace develops with Singarda and Distillation pressing Athenian Spirit, meaning the race is run at a stronger clip and those positioned second or third have cover and momentum entering the straight; horses who manage to secure a prominent pitch without burning energy early are the clear beneficiaries

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole opens the door for the deepest-lying horses
scenarios.body: A false pace forces a bunched field and the sprint finish theoretically suits closers, but this scenario is heavily discounted because so many supposed hold-up types are racing out of role and unlikely to be genuinely last off the bridle; should the speed collapse entirely, horses with the cleanest passage — not the deepest — benefit

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Suits Traveller
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the horse with the best cruising speed and lowest weight simply outstays rivals from mid-division
scenarios.body: With a dawdling gallop setting up a stamina test in disguise, lower-weighted horses who travel smoothly through the race without getting detached hold a marginal edge; this scenario depends on an unusually tardy pace and clear passage, neither of which is guaranteed

watchPoints.text: Athenian Spirit — if it gets an uncontested lead and no horse applies pressure through the early stages, it could dictate terms throughout and its redistribution to the front becomes a self-fulfilling tactical advantage.
Singarda and Distillation — both are likely to push forward from their natural positions, and if they press Athenian Spirit hard, the pace shape changes materially, opening the race up for closers.

Hear The Drums — flagged as a fader after 51 days off; if it comes under pressure before the straight on a circuit where there is no hiding place, it could spread interference through the hold-up group behind it.

Soda and Mist of Time — both genuine hold-up types packed into midfield on the map; watch whether Connor Beasley or Luke Morris find room turning for home, because traffic here could decide finishing positions without any merit involved.

Go Teejay — the combination of a hood (p, first time in this configuration), a 3lb claim from Jary, and a low draw warrants monitoring in the betting; a market move would suggest the headgear switch is expected to produce a different display.

runners_data.name: Ernie McCrew
runners_data.note: Moderate form string (646745) over this trip on Standard, jockey Ashley Lewis (3lb claimer) for J S Moore who sends three in the past fortnight; a genuine hold-up operator whose natural rear-division style is squeezed into midfield by the sheer number of closers in this field, which tempers confidence in a strong finish.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and fourth two starts back, Ernie McCrew arrives on a 16-day turnaround with experience over today's distance and going. He's yet to win in recent starts, but our rating of 57 edges him above his official mark, making him an interesting each-way proposition from stall six at 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Here Comes Louie
runners_data.note: Roger Fell runner flagged for fading late, a serious concern given two hold-up runs at this trip on Standard going that produced 8th and 10th; Kevin Stott's mount has tried a mile twice here without placing and the finishing tendency makes this a tough ask even if pace is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Here Comes Louie at least shaped with promise when second last time out, and he has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 131 lb from stall one, the concern is that sixth and eighth-place efforts earlier in the sequence suggest inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: Consistent form figures (123434) suggest a well-placed horse in ordinary handicaps but every recent run has come on Good or Soft turf — the Standard Fibresand surface is the key unknown here; by nature she wants to be produced late, yet the map has her in midfield because the field is packed with hold-up types, and J F Egan will need to improvise.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and a winner six starts back, Alice's Influence has experience of today's trip and going, but her last four outings have yielded only a pair of thirds, so she'll need to find improvement off a mark of 51 to challenge from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Gilleangirl
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes over for Ivan Furtado after a 121-day absence, and all three career starts have come on Standard Fibresand at this track; form figures of 5-8-7 over shorter trips (7f) suggest the step to a mile is an open question, and the tongue-tie adds a layer of uncertainty on return.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and returning after 121 days off, Gilleangirl has run over today's trip and going before and draws stall two carrying 135 lb — but a trainer striking at just 5% recently is the concern.

runners_data.name: Starakova
runners_data.note: The natural prominent runner in this field with a Southwell win over 7f on Standard to her name (1/7f/STA) and another place here; Harry Vigors (5lb claimer) rides for Warren Greatrex who has a runner in the past fortnight, and her ability to sit just behind Gloriola and travel into the race makes her the horse most logically positioned to exploit the steady pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Starakova showed she can win at this level with a victory three starts back, and her third last time out — 31 days ago — keeps her primed; the risk is that her seventh two starts back hints at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Elashgar
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost send out this lightly-raced colt who has stepped up in distance from sprint trips (5-6f) to 7f and now a mile; three wins at shorter on Standard suggest he handles Fibresand well, but the form question is whether his stamina extends to a flat mile and William Pyle must balance a hold-up tendency with the need to close ground.
runners_data.comment: Elashgar arrives here fit off a 21-day break, has run over today's trip and going, and shaped with promise when third last time out, with a win and a second also in recent starts — the concern is whether he can recapture that consistency after a couple of below-par efforts in between.

runners_data.name: Gloriola
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner: three of her five starts on Standard Fibresand here have produced a win and a place, and the uncontested lead on this flat track is a genuinely favourable setup for Clifford Lee and Steph Hollinshead; Hollinshead has sent no runners in the past 14 days (0/8) but Gloriola's course record and tactical advantage make her pivotal to the race shape regardless.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Gloriola faces a stiff task ranked seventh of nine on our figures, though at least she has run over today's distance and going before and arrives 30 days fresh — back-to-back placed efforts recently offer a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Speckled Brown
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh rides for Andi Brown, who sends only one runner in the fortnight window; a horse whose form (0-5-4-7) was all achieved on Good or Good-to-Soft ground, and whose hold-up style is pushed into a midfield role on the map simply because so many rear-runners populate this field — the combination of surface doubt and positional compromise makes this a difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked bottom on our figures, Speckled Brown faces a stiff task here; a fourth two starts back hints at some ability, she has run over today's trip before, and 18 days since her last outing leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Thomas Tallis
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and absent 65 days, John Mackie's runner has four career starts all producing finishes of 7th or worse; Callum Hutchinson rides, and while two of those efforts came on Standard Fibresand, the pattern of finishes offers little encouragement — mapped mid-pack rather than at his natural rear position, and the layoff adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Thomas Tallis has a tough task here; a run of sevenths and an unplaced effort offer little encouragement, though he has run over today's trip and going before and 65 days between starts at least leaves him fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Gloriola is the sole confirmed front-runner in a nine-runner field and, critically, faces no meaningful challenge for the lead — she can control tempo from the outset at a pace entirely of her own choosing on Standard Fibresand at Southwell. With only one horse genuinely looking to dictate, the gallop is likely to be measured rather than searching, which historically benefits those racing prominently in behind rather than deep closers who need a strong pace to close the gap. Starakova is the key prominent challenger and the horse most likely to sit just off Gloriola's shoulder in second or third, while Ernie McCrew, Alice's Influence, Speckled Brown and Thomas Tallis are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions on the map because there are simply too many rear-division types to place them all at the back — of the genuinely prominent types, Starakova is best placed to secure that tactical slot. The race shape strongly favours the lead-to-prominent profile: a lone, uncontested front-runner on a flat all-weather track with a steady pace and no natural pressers is a near-ideal setup for the horse who can travel close to the action and produce a sustained kick into the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gloriola Controls, Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Gloriola dictates an unchallenged, honest-but-not-searching pace and the field strings out steadily behind her.
scenarios.body: Gloriola's uncontested lead allows her to dictate every yard at Southwell's flat mile, and the horse sitting just off the pace in a tracking role arrives with reserves intact to collar her entering the final furlong; pure hold-up horses are left with too little ground to make up from their rear positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Gloriola Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sufficiently moderate that Gloriola conserves energy and outstays all challengers to the line.
scenarios.body: An uncontested, relaxed early gallop allows Gloriola to dictate every fraction and, with no rival able to close from a midfield/hold-up berth in time, she holds the rail and keeps pulling on the Fibresand surface to record a front-running win.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Fire Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens unexpectedly mid-race, stretching the field and leaving Gloriola vulnerable to a late flourish from behind.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-anticipated gallop would erode the front-runner's advantage and give the midfield horses a genuine pace to aim at — however, this scenario is materially discounted because the redistributed hold-up types (Ernie McCrew, Alice's Influence, Speckled Brown, Thomas Tallis) are racing out of their natural rear positions, meaning genuine late-finishing power is limited.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scrimmage, Scrappy Result
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems and jostling among the crowded midfield group disrupt several runners simultaneously, producing an unpredictable outcome.
scenarios.body: With four horses redistributed into an already-congested middle section, positional interference in the first half of the race could compromise multiple fancied runners and open the door to an opportunist result; Starakova, travelling prominently and cleanly, would be the least affected by such chaos.

watchPoints.text: Gloriola is the race-shaper — if Clifford Lee is able to dictate a completely uncontested lead from the front, the whole field is at her mercy and she controls the race from wire to wire.

Starakova is the one horse positioned to naturally track Gloriola throughout; if Harry Vigors (5lb claimer) allows a gap to open to the leader in the first half-mile, closing it on Fibresand against a relaxed front-runner becomes markedly harder.

Four redistributed hold-up horses (Ernie McCrew, Alice's Influence, Speckled Brown, Thomas Tallis) will be competing for the same midfield ground, raising the risk of traffic issues and positional friction in the early and middle stages of the race.

Here Comes Louie carries a specific flag for fading in the finish — in a race where pace is unlikely to be strong, Kevin Stott should be alert to covering ground early enough that a flat finish does not expose this tendency over the final two furlongs.

Gloriola's trainer Steph Hollinshead has no runners in the past 14 days (0/8); stable form is worth monitoring before the off, though Gloriola's tactical position as sole front-runner means she will set the terms regardless.

races.name: Simon Davis Big 60th Birthday Bash Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ravishing Beauty
runners_data.note: Consistent recent form (three places in last five including a win on Soft) suits a prominently-ridden strategy; genuine P-style horse with headgear noted, 20 days fresh, and her one Southwell AW run produced a place — handily positioned to take advantage if Hauteluce weakens.|
runners_data.comment: Ran third last time out and again two starts back, with a win three starts back keeping her claims alive, but ranked eighth of eleven here suggests she faces a stiff task from stall five carrying 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Hauteluce
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in this field; won at Southwell over 10f on Standard last time and drops back to a mile, giving her control of the tempo — her 0.93 style-fit confirms she is racing in her natural role and is the key pace influence throughout.|
runners_data.comment: Rated well below her official mark on our figures and ranked tenth of eleven, Hauteluce is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and a placed effort last time; the trainer's 28% strike rate and distance-and-going experience offer slim crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Filly Eilish
runners_data.note: In-form filly (1W3P in sim-going over this trip) whose natural tendency is to race prominently, but with several others also wanting to push forward, she is likely to find herself further back than ideal — De Sousa takes the ride which is an upgrade.|
runners_data.comment: Filly Eilish brings a recent win to the table and has run over today's trip and going before, but the trainer's lean spell — just one winner from 21 runners lately — is a concern for a filly carrying 135 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Zarinca
runners_data.note: Has winning form on Southwell AW at 6f and 7f and steps up to a mile; her P-style should see her in the chasing group, but her best form has come over shorter — the step up in trip is the key question here under Beasley.|
runners_data.comment: Zarinca landed a win four starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 78 putting her clear of her rivals at the head of this 11-runner field; from stall 3 off 20 days, she just needs to recapture that winning form.

runners_data.name: Dream Illusion
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with an excellent Standard-going record (3W7P in similar conditions), though her sim-going record at Southwell specifically is modest — Hart takes the ride and she is best served by a strong pace that stretches the field ahead of her.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last six starts, Dream Illusion does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a second two starts back keeps her honest; at 139 lb from stall 8, the weight is the obvious query for a filly ranked fifth of eleven.

runners_data.name: Kiss Me My Love
runners_data.note: Recent winner on Good and has placed five times in the last five at this trip but her Southwell AW sim-going record reads 0W0P in 15 runs, which is a significant concern despite her winning profile; Mason rides for Fell.|
runners_data.comment: Kiss Me My Love arrives on the back of a win eight days ago and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 72 marking her out as a leading threat; the main risk is that unplaced effort on her penultimate start.

runners_data.name: Kartini
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on Standard including a second at Southwell over 10f, and naturally wants to race close to the pace, but the prominent positions are likely already taken by Hauteluce and Ravishing Beauty — Eaves will need to be creative tactically.|
runners_data.comment: Kartini showed plenty of promise when a close second two starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going to call upon; the concern is that her most recent outing ended in a sixth, so she needs to bounce back from that.

runners_data.name: Court Of Stars
runners_data.note: Multiple places on Standard at Southwell in recent starts (1W3P sim-going) and is a P-style horse that should slot in neatly behind Hauteluce; Morris is an experienced Southwell operator and the 3yo filly's fresh record (LR 20 days) looks fine.|
runners_data.comment: Court of Stars arrives with experience over today's trip and going, and her second four starts back and win six starts back show she can compete at this level — the concern is that her last two outings have brought an unplaced effort and a sixth, suggesting she needs to rediscover that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Zermatt Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has run four consecutive losing runs including two on All-Weather; no similar-going form logged to assess — the most unknown quantity in the field and has to improve markedly on recent efforts.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Zermatt Star at least has experience over today's trip and a fourth last time out offers mild encouragement, though an official mark of 67 and a draw from stall 11 leave her needing to find improvement to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Blue Celestial
runners_data.note: Strong record of placing on Standard AW (6P in sim-going including two at Southwell) and is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, though the crowded rear of this field means she may need to manoeuvre through others — Clifford Lee for Tate is a stable that knows Southwell well.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Blue Celestial has been placed four times in that sequence but the sixth two starts back is the concern; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 127 lb from stall nine, and our rating ranks her ninth of eleven.

runners_data.name: Gifts Differing
runners_data.note: Longest absentee in the field at 54 days and has never won or placed in Standard-going runs on the AW; a genuine closer by style but her consistency has been poor and the layoff plus weak sim-going record makes her the hardest to recommend.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, all resulting in fifth or sixth, Gifts Differing faces a stiff ask ranked last on our figures here; the 54-day absence adds another query, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Hauteluce is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on a flat Southwell AW mile with standard going, she should establish a comfortable, uncontested lead from the outset and control the tempo throughout — her 0.93 style-fit score confirms she is genuinely built for this role. Behind her, Ravishing Beauty and Court Of Stars are the most likely to occupy the next prominent positions, with Zarinca also capable of tracking close to the pace. The middle section of the field is congested with horses whose natural inclinations have been displaced: Kartini, Filly Eilish, and Blue Celestial are all genuine prominent or hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their preferred position in this shape, reducing their chance in whichever scenario depends on that positioning. With one horse setting a sustainable, uncontested pace and a compressed chasing group, this race shape most clearly favours horses that can race handily just off the leader — prominent types with proven Standard going form — and those hold-up horses with a genuine late kick will need to find a way through a bunched midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hauteluce Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hauteluce bowls along in front without any meaningful pressure and the chasing pack cannot close the gap off a measured tempo.
scenarios.body: Hauteluce sets an uncontested, controlled pace on the front end and her recent win at Southwell over this trip on Standard gives her every right to be competitive here; horses racing prominently behind her — Ravishing Beauty and Court Of Stars — are best-placed to track and pick up any scraps.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Hauteluce's pace proves just slow enough that the closest pursuers are able to reel her in inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Ravishing Beauty, who won over this course and distance on Soft and has solid recent form, or Court Of Stars, who has placed multiple times on Standard at this track, could sustain a run from close range to collar the leader; this scenario rewards horses that have travelled comfortably in second or third throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a true closer can find a clear passage through the field.
scenarios.body: Dream Illusion and Kiss Me My Love are the most legitimate hold-up types in the race and both carry solid Standard-going records at this course; Kiss Me My Love in particular returned a recent win on Good and could produce a late rattle if gaps open — though both need the pace to be quicker than Hauteluce is likely to set.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses fight for positions behind Hauteluce, causing bunching and interference that scrambles the usual order.
scenarios.body: A congested midfield of displaced prominent types — Kartini, Filly Eilish — disrupting each other's rhythm could create a chaotic finish where a horse that finds daylight at the right moment wins opportunistically; this is a low-probability shape given Hauteluce's clear lead role, but the compressed pack makes minor incidents more likely than in a truly strung-out race.

watchPoints.text: Hauteluce's early gallop will set the entire complexion of the race — watch whether she is allowed to stride into a clear lead unchallenged or if Ravishing Beauty and Court Of Stars push her into a faster opening quarter than intended.

Kartini and Filly Eilish are both natural prominent types who cannot both get the position they want — watch for early scrimmaging or bumping in the first two furlongs as they jostle for the limited rail and tracking positions.

Kiss Me My Love's 0W0P record across 15 runs on Southwell AW Standard is a significant flag despite her winning recent form on Good; watch whether she can travel fluently on a surface that has previously not suited her.

Blue Celestial and Gifts Differing are both genuine hold-up types racing from a congested midfield — watch whether either can find a clear run approaching the home straight or whether they are repeatedly blocked by the bunched middle pack.

Dream Illusion has a strong 3W7P record in similar going but has not run over a full mile at Southwell AW — watch how Jason Hart positions her in the early stages to see if she is asked to travel closer than usual given the modest expected pace.

runners_data.name: Kodiac City
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes has a 14-day strike rate of 4/31 and sends out a debutant on unknown going; Kevin Stott is an astute jockey for positional races and an unclassified style means the horse could naturally settle prominent, which is exactly where this race will be won.

runners_data.name: Quest For Glory
runners_data.note: Two runs on this exact course and trip in Standard conditions (best effort a third), giving it a clear experience edge in this novice field; prominent style suits perfectly under the moderate pace Hoosthat will set, and Harry Vigors (5lb claimer) keeps the weight manageable.

runners_data.name: Vinery
runners_data.note: Placed over 6f on Good ground but faded to sixth on 7f at Goodwood last time — the step to a mile on Fibresand is an open question; hold-up style and uncertain distance stamina make this a spectator in the likely tactical shape.

runners_data.name: Hoosthat
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and therefore certain to get the lead from flag fall, but a fade-in-finish flag from its sole start (eighth on Good ground) is a genuine concern; 59 days off the track for Muir & Grassick and the lack of a presser may actually help it conserve enough energy to factor.

races.paceDynamic: Hoosthat is the lone confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner novice and, critically, carries a fade-in-finish flag — meaning the pace it sets is unlikely to be truly strong or sustained through the closing stages. With no genuine presser to challenge Hoosthat for the lead, the race will be run at a comfortable, controlled tempo from the front, with Quest For Glory likely to track closely from a prominent position. The moderate gallop this creates will compress the field and shorten the winning margin, suiting horses with tactical speed who can sit within two lengths of the pace and pounce before the line rather than those requiring a truly strong end-to-end gallop to deliver a late run. Hold-up horses such as Baarberini, Astral Crown, and Vinery are at a structural disadvantage here — the pace will not be strong enough to set them up for a sweeping finish off a fast final quarter. The field carries more hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear; Astral Crown is a genuine hold-up horse shown in midfield purely due to redistribution, and its chance must be discounted accordingly — Quest For Glory and the unexposed prominent types (Kodiac City, Phantom Knight) are best positioned to exploit the tactical shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Hoosthat dictates a moderate tempo and the race is won from the front two or three positions turning in.
scenarios.body: Hoosthat sets a comfortable gallop and the race becomes a tactical affair settled by who has the best finishing kick off a slow pace; prominent racers who track the leader throughout hold an immediate positional advantage over closers left with no pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Lands Gamble
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed newcomers (Phantom Knight, Kodiac City) shows raw ability to overcome inexperience and stalk the pace.
scenarios.body: With Standard going and a gentle tempo, a gifted newcomer with natural pace can take a prominent position without burning energy and pick up smartly; both Balding and Hughes send out well-prepared debutants who often hit the frame first time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hoosthat Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Hoosthat, despite its fade flag, is simply better than the field and the easy pace preserves enough energy to hold on.
scenarios.body: At a very modest gallop Hoosthat avoids the burn that caused its previous fade, and if rivals behind cannot accelerate quickly enough the leader steals it; a field low on proven quality makes this a live possibility despite the form concern.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Swooper Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and hold-up horses find daylight in time to finish through.
scenarios.body: This shape is the least likely given Hoosthat's confirmed tendency to fade rather than press on and the redistribution of Astral Crown out of its natural rear position; even if closers travel well, the lack of genuine gallop makes a winning late run improbable from this field.

watchPoints.text: Hoosthat sets the entire pace context — watch whether it bowls along to dominate or is content to dawdle, as even a small variance in tempo radically changes whether hold-up horses can get into the race.

Phantom Knight and Kodiac City are both debut runners from powerful stables (Balding, Hughes) — market moves before the off should be monitored closely as either could be significantly fancied and land a tactical position off a slow pace.

Astral Crown's redistribution means it will be racing out of its natural hold-up role; watch whether Daniel Tudhope attempts to push forward early to compensate, which would add unexpected pressure to Hoosthat and change the race shape entirely.

Quest For Glory has the clearest course-and-distance experience in the field on matching Standard AW going — in a race where inexperience is widespread, that positional familiarity under a 5lb claimer could be underestimated in the market.
Baarberini's trainer James Horton is 0 from 11 over the last 14 days — stable form is a real concern and should temper enthusiasm for what looks a capable individual on its single run.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Hectic
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse that has been pushed into a midfield slot on the pace map because the field's genuine closers outnumber available space at the rear; five of its last six runs are from off the pace and it showed interest at Southwell on standard going, but a 55-day layoff and a tendency to finish without winning limits confidence.
runners_data.comment: Hectic has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating puts him ahead of his official mark, suggesting he's better than the bare form; the concern is that he's been consistently out of the frame in recent starts and returns after 55 days.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen teams up for a trainer in strong 14-day form (4/24) and the horse has two placed efforts at Southwell on standard going in its recent history, making it one of the more credibly placed horses to sit just off the lone leader; a hold-up type by nature but compact enough to track from second or third.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Pickersgill is hard to fancy at these weights despite two recent runner-up efforts; she has experience over today's trip and going, and ten days between runs suggests she's ready, but the rating places her firmly at the bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Moostar
runners_data.note: De Sousa takes the ride for a trainer running at a healthy 13/58 strike rate over 14 days, and this four-year-old has hit the frame five times in 15 starts on standard going without winning; the horse is a genuine closer that the map has relocated into midfield, and its best chance relies on Ziggy's Condor coming back to the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, though a second two runs back shows she retains ability; Moostar has run over today's trip and going, but an eighth last time out is hard to ignore as she steps out from stall four carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Daytona Lady
runners_data.note: Has been to Southwell on standard going 13 of its last 15 recorded runs and the course suits it markedly — the best course-form profile in the race; a natural hold-up type whose redistribution into midfield on the map reflects the overcrowded rear of this field, not a change in how it will race.

runners_data.name: Court Drive
runners_data.note: Wore blinkers last time and produced a winning effort at 6f on soft, suggesting headgear has sharpened it up; Gay Kelleway's two-runner 14-day book is thin but the horse has placed at Southwell on standard ground and it operates as a hold-up type, squeezed toward midfield on the map by the volume of closers in this race.
runners_data.comment: Court Drive has winning form in her recent starts — a winner three starts back — but her latest two outings have produced a third two starts back and a fourth last time out, suggesting she's finding it tough to land a blow; she has run over today's distance and going before, and 24 days off looks a fair freshener.

runners_data.name: Ottawa
runners_data.note: 173 days off the track is a significant fitness concern here, and although it won at Southwell on standard going it has also finished sixth twice on the same surface since; Daniel Tudhope is a top jockey booking but the layoff and inconsistent Southwell record temper expectations — operates from hold-up to midfield.
runners_data.comment: Ottawa has been out of the plate for 173 days and has finished fifth or worse in his last three starts, making him hard to fancy ranked bottom of the field on our figures. He has run over today's distance and going before, and a win four starts back offers slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Showtime Mahomes
runners_data.note: 163 days absent makes this a tough assignment, and the seven-year-old's last win came at Southwell on standard going but that is now some way back; a hold-up type that has been mapped into midfield because of the crowded rear, and returning from such a break into a competitive handicap on the all-weather requires a big fitness leap.
runners_data.comment: A 163-day absence and an unplaced last effort make Showtime Mahomes hard to fancy here, ranked eighth of ten on our figures; he does have experience of today's trip and going, and draw two is noted, but there's plenty to prove on his recent form.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Condor
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and the axis around which the entire pace map rotates; James Doyle is a significant jockey upgrade and the horse wears a visor, ran just five days ago suggesting fitness is fine, and its OR of 70 makes it the top-rated runner — the key question is whether Doyle presses home the tactical advantage of being uncontested.
runners_data.comment: Ziggy's Condor shaped well when third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 79 marks him as a serious threat from stall one carrying 135 lb — the main concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Cairdeas
runners_data.note: Has gone close twice at Southwell in 15 starts on standard going and David Nolan retains the ride after a 10-day turnaround; the horse races as a genuine hold-up type but its Southwell experience and ability to travel smoothly positions it as one of the natural default trackers behind Ziggy's Condor in a field short of pace.
runners_data.comment: Cairdeas has run over today's trip and going, and his two runner-up finishes in recent starts show he can threaten at this level; the concern is a trainer who is yet to land one from 21 runners in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Miraculous
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's horse has only three runs from 15 on standard going that have yielded any place money and none have come at Southwell, making this a surface and course query; David Allan rides but the lack of Fibresand form, a recent string of mid-to-rear finishes and a hold-up profile in the wrong race shape all count against.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Miraculous heads the rankings on a rating of 82 and brings experience over today's trip and conditions, but his recent string of eighth and seventh suggests he faces a stiff task from stall three carrying 134 lb for a trainer in lean form.

races.paceDynamic: Ziggy's Condor is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 6f Southwell handicap and, with no serious rival to dispute the lead, James Doyle can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on standard-going Fibresand. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Hectic, Moostar, Daytona Lady, Court Drive, Ottawa, and Showtime Mahomes are all true closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than they prefer simply because there is no genuine pace for them to track. This field contains far more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, and those most likely to actually secure a prominent tracking position behind Ziggy's Condor are Pickersgill and Cairdeas, who have the profile and course form to slot in early. The race shape firmly favours a horse that can track the lone leader at close quarters and produce a sustained run into the straight, rather than a pure closer launching from far back against a potentially uncontested and metronomic pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Condor bowls along uncontested and sets a measured, honest gallop that suits its stamina.
scenarios.body: Doyle dictates every yard on standard Fibresand, and the holding-up pack is simply left with too much ground to make up in the final two furlongs against a horse that has never been asked to quicken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Trackers Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Pickersgill or Cairdeas track Ziggy's Condor at a length or two and time their run to nail the front-runner close home.
scenarios.body: A genuine close-tracking position from just off the pace is the premium spot in this race given the single pace-setter, and these two have the Southwell course form and profile to exploit it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If Ziggy's Condor overcooks the early pace or ties up late, allowing a well-placed hold-up horse to run through.
scenarios.body: Daytona Lady has exceptional course form at Southwell and handles standard going better than almost anyone in the field, making her the most credible beneficiary if the front-runner does not get the race run to suit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If a contested early gallop develops despite the apparent lack of rivals and the field becomes strung out with no clear beneficiary.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability chaos scenario in which unconsidered hold-up types who find cover early could emerge late, but the redistribution of so many closers into an unnatural prominent position makes it an unlikely and messy outcome.

watchPoints.text: Ziggy's Condor sets the entire race tempo alone — watch whether James Doyle elects to press on and build a lead or sit in a comfort zone, as that decision will determine whether closers have any chance of getting back.

Pickersgill and Cairdeas are the two hold-up types most likely to break from their natural role and slot in just behind the leader — if either gets a clean passage to track Ziggy's Condor within two lengths, they become the most dangerous runners in the race.

Daytona Lady's 13-from-15 course-going profile on Southwell standard is exceptional and makes it the standout closer in the field — watch whether James Sullivan gets a clear run from the two-furlong pole if the front-runner flattens out.

Ottawa (173 days off) and Showtime Mahomes (163 days off) are both returning from lengthy breaks — monitor market moves before the off, as both could be unconsidered if connections have done quiet work at home, but the layoffs are a genuine caution.

Court Drive's recent blinkers application has coincided with improved form including a win, and Gay Kelleway's yard is quiet over 14 days — if the headgear has a continued sharpening effect, it could outperform its OR of 63 from a midfield position.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Fierce
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Paul Midgley who handles Standard Southwell well (8 runs, 1W 3P in similar going); Jason Hart takes the ride and the 6f trip suits, though getting competitive from deep in a compressed field is the key challenge.
runners_data.comment: Fierce has been placing consistently in recent starts — third two runs back and second three runs back — and he has experience of today's distance and going, while his rating of 77 tops the field; the risks are a 41-day absence and a trainer without a winner in 21 attempts over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Baba Reza
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee partners this consistent but ageing eight-year-old who has placed three times on Standard Southwell; his natural finishing kick from the rear is his weapon, but with the race map pushing him into midfield rather than his true rearward position, he may not get the run of the race he needs.
runners_data.comment: Baba Reza has been placed in three of his last five starts, finishing third last time out and second two starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions. Carrying 132 lb from stall six is the chief concern for a horse yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Jesse Luc
runners_data.note: Two wins and seven places from 14 starts on Standard going makes him statistically the most course-and-going-proven runner in the field; Luke Morris rides and the tongue piece is on, but as a genuine hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield slot he will need a stronger gallop than Sarafina Mshairi is likely to set to deliver his best.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts, Jesse Luc does offer two thirds in recent form as encouragement, though fifths and sixths pepper the record too; drawn three and carrying 131 lb, he has experience of today's trip and going, leaving him a credible if unspectacular midfield proposition.

runners_data.name: Sarafina Mshairi
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner — a 49-day break is a minor query but Edward Smyth-Osbourne sends her to Southwell where she won over this exact 6f trip on Standard ground; apprentice Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) keeps costs down and with no pace rival she has every chance to make this a one-act affair.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive eighths and ninths in her last two starts make Sarafina Mshairi hard to fancy, and she sits ranked seventh of nine on our figures; she does bring winning form from three starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, but much more is needed here.

runners_data.name: Camera Shy
runners_data.note: Won over 7f at Southwell and returns after a 93-day break for Michael Dods who is in strong 14-day form (3/27); cheekpieces on, but dropping to 6f from his habitual 7f trips is a concern, and as a true hold-up horse awkwardly mapped into a midfield role, his best form may not be reproducible here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and winless in his last three starts, Camera Shy faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's trip and going before and that sole win four starts back shows ability on a good day.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's charge has been running consistently in similar company and returns just 14 days after his last run, which is a positive fitness indicator; races in a tongue tie and maps as a genuine prominent racer, which suits this race shape well — the key question is whether his Southwell form over 7f translates to this sharper 6f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts with an unplaced effort most recently, Fan Mail faces a stiff ask from stall nine carrying 128 lb, and a trainer striking at just 4% over the past fortnight makes it hard to fancy, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Beattie Is Back
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse for the Fahey stable who has failed to score on similar going in his last six; Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim partially offsets the top weight of 135lbs, but a string of poor recent efforts on Standard ground makes it hard to construct a winning scenario.
runners_data.comment: Beattie Is Back shaped with promise when second five starts back and our rating of 75 ranks him second of nine here, making him a genuine threat despite being winless in recent starts; the single concern is a trainer without a winner in 42 attempts over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's five-year-old won over 6f on Good going relatively recently and Daniel Tudhope is a significant booking; the 93-day break is concerning and his Standard Southwell figures are modest (0W 1P from 6), but his best form would make him competitive if he returns to peak fitness.
runners_data.comment: Dorney Lake showed his best when winning three starts back and filling the runner-up spot two starts back, but has been unplaced most recently. He has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 13 days gives fair freshness — though 134 lb is a stern test at OR 69.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jenny
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello pairs with this lightly-raced four-year-old who won at Southwell over 6f on Standard going — the most relevant course-and-distance form in the field; a 73-day break is worth monitoring, but a horse that has already shown she handles this exact scenario could be well-placed tracking the pace throughout.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and a winner two starts back, Spirit Of Jenny arrives on the back of solid recent form and has run over today's trip and going before. Carrying 133 lb from stall five, the 73-day absence is the one query, but her profile makes her our pick here.

races.paceDynamic: Sarafina Mshairi is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 6f handicap on Southwell's flat Fibresand surface, and with no credible rival likely to push her from the front, she is set to control a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the gate. Fan Mail and Spirit Of Jenny will press forward into prominent positions just behind her, creating a structured but not frantically contested tempo. This race shape — a measured lead with a small group pressing just off the pace — typically rewards prominent racers who can travel into the race and quicken late off a true pace rather than deep closers relying on a strong injection of pace from behind. Three runners — Baba Reza, Jesse Luc, and Camera Shy — are genuine hold-up horses repositioned to midfield on the map because there are more true rear-of-field types in this field than the race shape can accommodate at the back; of these, Sarafina Mshairi is best placed to secure her natural lead, while Fan Mail and Spirit Of Jenny are most likely to claim the prominent slots ahead of the true closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sarafina Mshairi Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sarafina Mshairi secures an uncontested lead and the pace stays honest but not punishing throughout the 6f.
scenarios.body: She dictates from the front, sets a sustainable rhythm on Standard going, and proves hardest to reel in as no rival can muster a sustained challenge from deep; Fan Mail or Spirit Of Jenny, tracking closely in second or third, are ideally placed to benefit if she tires in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fan Mail or Spirit Of Jenny track the pace closely and find more than the leader in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With Sarafina Mshairi setting a manageable pace, a horse sitting a length or two off the lead travelling well can produce a decisive kick in the straight; both Fan Mail (tongue tie, recent run) and Spirit Of Jenny (won at Southwell, back from 73 days) suit this shape well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is hot enough to take a toll on Sarafina Mshairi and the prominent group, allowing late finishers to close.
scenarios.body: Jesse Luc and Fierce, both comfortable on Standard going with strong course records, would be the most likely beneficiaries as they close through tired horses; however this scenario depends on genuinely testing early fractions that are not obviously forthcoming given the lone front-runner dynamic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If scrimmaging for position early scrambles the race order and the midfield hold-up horses fail to find clear daylight.
scenarios.body: Baba Reza and Camera Shy, both racing out of their natural rear-of-field role due to the field composition, face the hardest task in finding the gaps they need; Dorney Lake, who has a recent course win and is ridden by Tudhope, represents the best chance of an upset from this unlikely scenario.

watchPoints.text: Sarafina Mshairi's early handling is critical — if Ashley Lewis (3) allows her to stride out without a fight for the lead, she could prove very difficult to catch at 6f on Standard Southwell with no pace rival in sight.
Spirit Of Jenny returns from 73 days off and won at Southwell over this exact course and distance on Standard going — watch market moves at the off to gauge stable confidence after the layoff.

Jesse Luc's redistribution out of his natural hold-up position means he is unlikely to get the strong gallop he needs to deliver his best; if the pace is modest, his chance is structurally undermined regardless of his strong course-and-going figures.
Camera Shy drops back from 7f to 6f after 93 days off — watch for signs of rustiness or reluctance to quicken on the shorter, sharper Southwell trip, as his best form has come over a longer distance.

Beattie Is Back carries the top weight of 135lbs for a yard that has recorded 0 wins from 40 runners in the last 14 days; if the market shortens him, treat with caution given the stable's current form.

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Astro King
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old hold-up specialist from Kubler, absent 55 days, whose recent form reads 4-9-0-0-0 — nothing in the figures screams confidence, and at OR 97 he is towards the top of the weight without the current form to justify optimism; the closing style is further disadvantaged by the steady pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Astro King nonetheless catches the eye on ratings and has run over today's trip and going before; drawn in stall one carrying 131 lb, he returns after 55 days off and looks the one to beat on a performance-level basis.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: Arrives on a short 9-day turnaround for David Evans, but that stable runs horses back quickly with purpose; brings a course win (1/10f/GOO) and holds sim-going form of 3W4P, making him the standout tracker profile, and a blindfold is noted as potential headgear addition.
runners_data.comment: King's Code won two starts back but has been beaten in his other five recent starts, including eighth last time out; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating edges above his official mark, though consistency remains the question at 129 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Ultrasoul
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old arrives on the back of three consecutive wins including two on Standard AW, and though returning from 54 days off, sim-going stats of 1W3P tell a compelling story; C Y Ho is a competent replacement booking and the horse is firmly progressive.
runners_data.comment: Ultrasoul arrives on the back of a hat-trick of wins and clearly in excellent nick, though 54 days off the track raises a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a trainer firing at 41% is a significant plus from stall 12 off 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Let's Dream
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's five-year-old is a genuinely prominent-running type by nature, but the crowded pace map means he is pushed into a midfield slot he won't relish — his last two wins came from forward positions and his style fit here is compromised (STYLE_FIT=0.93); treat any chance accordingly.
runners_data.comment: He has run over today's trip and shown he can win, with back-to-back victories three and four starts back, but his last two runs have been well below that level; a trainer strike-rate of just 4% in the past fortnight is an additional concern despite a rating of 96 suggesting residual ability.

runners_data.name: Port Of London
runners_data.note: A notable returnee from 227 days off for the Gosden yard — headgear of a paceband noted — and his sim-going figures of 2W3P on Standard (4/5 runs) are excellent, but he is a natural front-runner being squeezed into midfield by the crowded pace map, which blunts his effectiveness; Robert Havlin will need fortune to find the right position.
runners_data.comment: Port Of London won two of his last five starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but 227 days off the track is a significant concern, and stall 13 is his draw from 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Say What You See
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with back-to-back wins (12f and 10f) in recent form and a paceband noted; Luke Morris will settle him at the rear and hunt the gaps, but on a flat Standard track with a single, measured pace-setter, he needs the leader to come back to him — the race shape doesn't favour a late charge unless something breaks down.
runners_data.comment: A 55-day absence and a ranking of ninth of thirteen make him hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins in his last two starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, but fresher rivals are likely to pose a stiff test from stall eight off 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Speaking
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa's mount has won twice on Standard AW at shorter trips (7f), but 1m3f is a significant step in distance; naturally wants to race prominently, but is displaced into midfield by the pace traffic, and sim-going at this course shows only 1W1P from 15 Standard runs — the style mismatch and trip concern combine to limit expectations.
runners_data.comment: Jimmy Speaking has tumbled to fourth and ninth in his last two starts, making him hard to fancy ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, though he does bring winning form from earlier in this sequence and has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Cloth Of Gold
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen's four-year-old for Charlie Johnston has a win on Standard AW (1/10f/STA) and returns fresh off 20 days; a natural hold-up horse with sim-going stats of 1W4P, he needs cut in the pace that a lone, unhurried Spinning Wheel may not provide, leaving him vulnerable to one-paced closing efforts.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Cloth Of Gold has finished fourth and seventh in his last two starts, with his sole recent win coming five starts back. Experience over today's trip and going and a reasonable turnaround of 20 days offer little rescue at 117 lb.

runners_data.name: Per Contra
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's gelding has a paceband and modest recent figures (4th at best), and 19 days between runs is fine, but sim-going of 1W2P from 15 Standard runs illustrates a horse that rarely fires here; Duran Fentiman has limited room to work with from the rear of a 13-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with an unplaced effort two runs back and nothing better than third in recent outings, Per Contra is hard to fancy — a trainer striking at just 4% over the past 14 days compounds the concern, despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Virtual Rock
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 104 but returns from a staggering 741-day layoff — no amount of class fully compensates for that absence, and his sim-going record of 0W2P on Standard is a secondary concern; Connor Beasley must manage a rusty, big-framed seven-year-old from the front of the handicap.
runners_data.comment: Long off the track after 741 days away, Virtual Rock returns with an open profile — a winner in recent starts, and a third and runner-up also on his card. Unexposed and open to improvement, he'll need to strip fit on this comeback.

runners_data.name: Spinning Wheel
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner at OR 102 from Simon & Ed Crisford; LR 61 days but fit enough for a straightforward lead role on Standard Fibresand, a surface he handles well, and 1m3f sits squarely in his winning range — the pace-setter to anchor all scenario thinking.
runners_data.comment: Spinning Wheel showed smart form when winning three starts back and running second four starts back, giving him a strong recent profile over today's trip; the main concern is whether 61 days off the track has left him ring-rusty.

runners_data.name: El Burhan
runners_data.note: George Boughey's gelding carries a tongue-tie and has 90 days since last seen, but sim-going record of 1W on Standard (the solitary outing) and an OR of 99 suggest latent ability; Jack Callan needs a clean run from a prominent pitch that may be crowded early.
runners_data.comment: El Burhan's win three starts back marks him as a live contender on a mark of 99, and he has run over today's trip — his rating of 101 ranks him fourth of 13. The main risk is a 90-day absence, which leaves his sharpness open to question.

runners_data.name: French Duke
runners_data.note: James Doyle is a strong booking for Hamad Al Jehani's charge, and a win over 12f suits this step up; however zero wins from 13 attempts on Standard going is a glaring flag and the wide draw may compound problems in a full field.
runners_data.comment: French Duke showed his best when winning four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going keeps him firmly in the picture off 132 lb — the concern is that he has finished sixth twice in his last three starts, suggesting he needs to reproduce that better form.

races.paceDynamic: Spinning Wheel is the lone confirmed front-runner and, uncontested on the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Southwell's flat fibresand track over 1m3f — a trip that suits a horse who has won and placed at the distance on similar surfaces. With no genuine challenger for the lead, Oisin Orr can dictate every yard at a pace that suits his mount, draining the finish from those who must chase. The three redistributed runners — Let's Dream, Port Of London, and Jimmy Speaking — are all naturally prominent types who will be pushed back into midfield positions that are foreign to their usual racing patterns, meaning the principal challengers will come from the genuine hold-up horses (Astro King, Say What You See, Cloth Of Gold, Per Contra) and the more classily-rated prominent types Virtual Rock, El Burhan, French Duke, Ultrasoul, and King's Code, who must work to secure their berths. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the pace map can accommodate, and Spinning Wheel is overwhelmingly likely to be the sole pace-setter; Let's Dream and King's Code are best-placed of the prominent pack to at least track close early. The race shape strongly favours Spinning Wheel and any prominent or progressive horse comfortable sitting just off a controlled pace on Standard Fibresand — hold-up horses face the stiffest task conceding a free run to the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Spinning Wheel Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Spinning Wheel secures the lead uncontested and sets a comfortable, metronomic gallop that stretches the field without burning energy.
scenarios.body: Oisin Orr dictates every fraction, and with no genuine rival pressing him, Spinning Wheel can balance beautifully through the race and quicken from the front over the final two furlongs; at OR 102 from the Crisford yard he carries class as well as positional advantage. Horses sitting just off the pace in genuine tracking positions — King's Code, Ultrasoul, El Burhan — are best placed to mount a challenge, but the leader's head-start in energy conservation is decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Wears Leader Down
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent trackers (King's Code, Ultrasoul, or El Burhan) settles just behind Spinning Wheel and outstays him over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Spinning Wheel's recent form shows vulnerability at the finish (twice second, twice in double figures), and a fresh horse sitting a length off through a sensible pace may well have more left at the two-pole; the 1m3f flat Southwell circuit can expose a front-runner who has no accelerant left. King's Code brings course-and-distance form (1/10f/GOO) and Ultrasoul is unbeaten in three in a row and thriving, making both the natural beneficiaries of this stalking shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight — perhaps Spinning Wheel over-exerts mid-race — allowing a genuine closer to power through from the back.
scenarios.body: Say What You See and Cloth Of Gold are the truest closers in the field with recent winning form, but both need the race to truly come back to them; on a flat Standard surface with a single controlled pace-setter, the deficit they must make up is substantial. Port Of London, despite being redistributed from its natural prominent position, carries strong surface form (2W3P on this going) and could be the one who punches through if a gap materialises near the inside.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Spinning Wheel loses the plot under pressure from the jumbled prominent pack early, creating a strung-out, falsely-run race that benefits an unexpected shape.
scenarios.body: With three naturally prominent horses (Let's Dream, Port Of London, Jimmy Speaking) struggling to find their rhythm from unfamiliar midfield berths, there could be early shuffling and erratic fractions if any of them push forward; this chaotic scenario most benefits Virtual Rock, who returns from 741 days off with a high OR of 104 and could exploit a muddled pace if fit enough. French Duke, who won over 12f on Good ground, might also find an opening in a disorganised race, though his Southwell record (0W on Standard) tempers confidence.

watchPoints.text: Virtual Rock's 741-day absence is the single largest unknown in the race — if he shows any ring rust early, Connor Beasley may be unable to settle him in a prominent pitch, potentially disrupting the pace map for Spinning Wheel and the tracking pack.

Let's Dream, Port Of London, and Jimmy Speaking are all natural prominent types crammed into midfield — watch for early jostling as two or more of them attempt to push forward to their preferred position, which could create a bunching incident on the first turn.

Spinning Wheel's recent form includes two clear-cut defeats (12th on Soft, 11th on Good) that bookend his wins — if the Crisford stable has not resolved whatever caused those blowouts, the presumed pace-setter may not perform his role reliably, dismantling the dominant scenario.

French Duke's zero wins from 13 Standard-going starts is a striking statistic for a horse at OR 98 in this market — if James Doyle attempts to compensate by sending him forward aggressively early, he could complicate Spinning Wheel's otherwise uncontested lead.

Port Of London's 227-day layoff combined with his natural front-running style being displaced to midfield makes him worth monitoring in the final furlong — if the Gosden yard have him spot-on, he could produce a sustained run through beaten horses that looks better than the race shape suggested it would.
